I'm not sure how much you know so I'm basically going to deconstruct my thoughts on the Beta.

The matchmaking is godawful. Lots of hangs etc. Not sure if it's because of a high volume of traffic, but I wouldn't instantly write it off on that. The Battlefront Beta, at least for me, had virtually no connection issues, and that was EA's biggest beta turnout or something.

I haven't followed Siege tremendously because AAA titles aren't my exact go-to, but there's two modes (at least in the Beta) - Terrorist Hunt and 'Multiplayer'.

Terrorist Hunt is you and up to 4 others (or just you) going to one of the designated maps and attempting to disarm the bombs on site. All the enemies are AI, and you can choose the difficulty they are (Normal, Hard and Realistic - I only played on Normal because it was hard enough). The reason I say that is because I think Terrorist Hunt is unbalanced in favour of the AI. As soon as you plant the defuser, more AI spawn outside (unrealistic because there would be all police outside), so I personally feel the mode is tacked on. You can do a private game with friends, and no time limit means you can properly identify threats, good pouts of entry etc - all the more better because you're chatting with friends.

'Multiplayer' is basically 5v5. A 30 second prep phrase at the beginning lets the Defenders set up barricades, barbed wire, reinforcements, etc, whilst the Attackers scout out with drones to see where shit is etc.

You select an 'Operator' you've unlocked with your Rainbow Six dollars, or go with the standard 'recruit'. The Operators all have some sort of special ability (for example, the hot FBI brunette has a grenade launcher that can fire into walls etc with a 5ish second delay, but you can't play as her when you're defending - there's 2 types of Operator). I think it works because if your favourite Operator is chosen, then you can pick another, and aren't left completely out to dry. Some are more useful than others, like one who can self-revive and heal others, but just about everybody can hold their own.

What I do like are the breach charges. You plant them on vulnerable surfaces and make your own door. They're useful not just in that, but for example, drawing the enemy player's attention elsewhere, or opening new sightlines as you eye up the best way to attack, along with their primary function of making new doors.

The gameplay feels fairly fluid, although I don't like how 5v5 Siege has a time limit to how long is left (I think it's maybe 2/3 minutes including the 30 secs 'preparation' phase). There's a point where the game crosses from fun to too realistic, and I'm not saying it should, but real life sieges easily last hours. I'm not saying RS Siege should copy that and have no timer, but I think that having one so short makes things a bit too fast paced for my liking.

On the standard review notes, the graphics are pretty good, the sound is alright, and the gunplay is fairly standard. This is all personal preference, so I won't write much, although there's nothing to write home about.

It's fairly solid overall. I just feel like its trying too hard to mimic CSGO's Competitive mode, but I appreciate the different spin they've got on it. It's fun if you have a few friends, but it's not hard to earn the points to unlock the Operators, so they'll have to make the post-launch Season Pass worth it to make people stay.

I'd wait for a good deal on it myself, although the Beta genuinely surprised me at actually how alright it was.
